To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

polyoma virus medium (large) T antigen forms a complex with a cellular protein of approximately 61,000 daltons (61K) and that this complex is found in cells infected with wild-type virus but not with a virus with a mutation in its large T gene.
the medium T antigen of polyoma virus, like the small t antigen, forms complexes with cellular proteins.
polyoma virus medium (middle) T antigen forms two complexes with cellular proteins, one of them being with a 61-kDa cellular protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cellular proteins that interact with polyoma virus medium and small T antigens.
the purification of medium T antigen from cell lysates by affinity chromatography with antibodies against two synthetic peptides.
the identification of cellular proteins that interact with polyoma virus medium and large T antigens and with the role of these interactions in the viral life cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polyoma medium T antigen forms complexes with cellular proteins that are involved in cell transformation and cell growth.
the medium T antigen of polyoma virus interacts with a number of cellular proteins, including pp60c-src, and that these interactions are required for the virus to transform cells.
the medium T antigen of polyoma virus interacts with at least three different cellular proteins, pp60v-src, a 61-kDa cellular protein, and a 72-kDa protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polyoma virus medium-T protein forms a complex with two cellular proteins of 61 and 72 kDa.
polyoma virus medium-T antigen forms complexes with at least three cellular proteins.
medium T antigen forms two different complexes with cellular proteins, and that the complexes formed with pp60c-src or the 61-kDa cellular protein may play a role in transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 61-kDa complex is present in extracts from cells transformed by the wild-type virus but not by the mutant NG59 virus and that the 61 kDa protein is a new cellular protein which forms a complex with medium T antigen.
the polyoma virus T antigen is a multifunctional protein that interacts with a variety of cellular proteins.
the 61-kDa complex was not detected in the extracts of transformed cells that had been treated with anti-mitotic drugs.
